entities.summary:
Attalus of Rhodes (b. 200 BCE, Rhodes) was a prominent logician and mathematician of the Classical era, active in Rhodes.

 Attalus of Rhodes was a student of the famous philosopher, Aristarchus of Samos, and later became a tutor to the mathematician, Eratosthenes of Cyrene. His contributions to the field of geometry, particularly in the development of the method of exhaustion, had a lasting impact on the work of later mathematicians such as Euclid.

 Attalus' work also had significant implications for the development of astronomical knowledge, as his student, Hipparchus of Rhodes, made major contributions to the field of trigonometry and the measurement of the Earth's circumference.

 Attalus' legacy extends beyond the Classical era, as his methods and discoveries influenced the work of later scholars, including the Arab mathematician, Al-Khwarizmi, who in turn passed on his knowledge to European scholars during the Middle Ages.

 The calculation of pi (π) remains a testament to Attalus' ingenuity, as his method of exhaustion was used to calculate the value of pi for the first time in ancient Greece.

 Attalus of Rhodes' impact on the development of mathematics and astronomy can be seen in the many schools and institutions that were established in his name, including the Attalus School of Mathematics in Alexandria.
